timing: Added after comparison-001 results were inspected; this is an explanatory control, not a preregistered discovery or a new blind validation.
observation: Sparse latent statistics generally lose sensitivity. Mixing candidate 08 with the Berk-Jones-style statistic improves IAAFT but reduces several other diagnostic scores.
confound: Adding another summary-derived component also increases the ensemble's weight on summaries relative to its field component. Improvement need not come from the sparse statistic itself.
controls: Mix candidate 08 with its existing raw summary energy, using exactly the same normal scaling and mean/max rules.
Compare the Berk-Jones mean ensemble against this matched dense-energy mean ensemble with paired bootstrap intervals.

Apply four fixed seeded orthogonal rotations to each model's standardized latent coordinates. Verify exact energy invariance and report maximum-coordinate score sensitivity to this arbitrary representation change. No rotation is selected for deployment.
public_test: Not read. No new submission candidate is chosen by these controls.
interpretation: These experiments assess mechanisms in the frozen learned representation. They cannot exclude sparse physical anomalies expressed in a different representation.
